entities.name: initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM)

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd
requirements.canonical: The `rnd` function has the signature `rnd([in float seed]) return float`, with an optional `in` formal parameter `seed` of type `float` and a return value of type `float`.
requirements.original: rnd([in float seed]) return float

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd
requirements.canonical: The `rnd` function returns a (pseudo) random `float` value that is greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1.
requirements.original: The rnd function returns a (pseudo) random number less than 1 but greater or equal to 0.

requirements.subject: ent:random-number-generator
requirements.canonical: The random number generator used by `rnd` IS initialized separately per test component and per module control function.
requirements.original: The random number generator is initialized per test component and for the control part by means of an optional seed value (a numerical float value).

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd
requirements.canonical: The random number generator of `rnd` MAY be initialized by passing an optional seed value of type `float` as actual parameter of `rnd`.
requirements.original: The random number generator is initialized per test component and for the control part by means of an optional seed value (a numerical float value).

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd
requirements.canonical: If `rnd` is called without a new seed value, the last random number generated by `rnd` IS used as seed for the next random number.
requirements.original: If no new seed is provided, the last generated number will be used as seed for the next random number.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether this is an observable rule (re-seeding with the last returned value) or an informal description of the generator state continuing; the first reading was chosen as it is the literal one.
readings: A call `rnd()` IS equivalent to `rnd(r)`, where r is the last value returned by `rnd` in the same test component or module control function.
A call `rnd()` IS the continuation of the current pseudo random sequence, with the generator-internal state acting as seed; the returned value need not equal `rnd(r)`.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd
requirements.condition: no previous initialization of the random number generator
requirements.canonical: If the random number generator has not been initialized with a seed value, a seed value calculated from the system time IS used when `rnd` is called for the first time in a test component or in the module control function.
requirements.original: Without a previous initialization a value calculated from the system time will be used as seed value when rnd is used the first time in a test component or the control part.

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd
requirements.condition: rnd is initialized with the same seed value
requirements.canonical: Each time `rnd` is initialized with the same seed value, `rnd` SHALL repeat the same sequence of random numbers.
requirements.original: Each time the rnd function is initialized with the same seed value, it shall repeat the same sequence of random numbers.

requirements.subject: ent:random-number-generator
requirements.canonical: Each test component and the module control function has its own random seed, to keep parallel testing deterministic.
requirements.original: NOTE: For the purpose of keeping parallel testing deterministic, each test component, as well as the control part has its own random seed.

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.subject: ent:random-number-generator
requirements.canonical: A separate random seed per test component and module control function allows for better reproducibility of test executions.
requirements.original: This allows for better reproducibility of test executions.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd
requirements.canonical: The `rnd` function always uses the seed of the test component or module control function that calls it.
requirements.original: Thus, the rnd function will always use the seed of the component or control part which calls it.

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd
requirements.canonical: A random integer in the range lowerbound..upperbound CAN be produced with the expression `float2int(int2float(upperbound - lowerbound + 1) * rnd()) + lowerbound`.
requirements.original: To produce a random integers in a given range, the following formula can be used: float2int(int2float(upperbound - lowerbound +1)*rnd()) + lowerbound

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of predefined functions defined in clause 16.1.2 apply to `rnd`.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-rnd
requirements.canonical: If the seed actual parameter of `rnd` is `infinity`, `-infinity` or `not_a_number`, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: seed is infinity, -infinity or not_a_number.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-testcasename
requirements.canonical: The `testcasename` function has the signature `testcasename() return charstring`, with no formal parameters and a return value of type `charstring`.
requirements.original: testcasename() return charstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-testcasename
requirements.canonical: The `testcasename` function SHALL return the unqualified name of the currently executing test case, also when called by a parallel test component.
requirements.original: The testcasename function shall return the unqualified name of the actually executing test case.

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-8 coding scheme IS EF BB BF.
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-8; initial octet sequence: EF BB BF; comments: signature not required / no effect

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: For UTF-8, the initial octet sequence (BOM) is not required and IS of no effect as a signature.
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-8; initial octet sequence: EF BB BF; comments: signature not required / no effect

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-16BE coding scheme IS FE FF.
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16BE; initial octet sequence: FE FF; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: For UTF-16BE, the octet sequence FE FF IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16BE; initial octet sequence: FE FF; comments: no signature meaning

ambiguity.issue: 'no signature meaning' does not say whether FE FF at the start of UTF-16BE data is treated as a ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE character (and therefore kept by `remove_bom`) or is still removed as a BOM; the first reading was chosen as it follows Unicode practice.
readings: For UTF-16BE, a leading FE FF IS NOT a BOM, and `remove_bom` IS NOT required to remove it.
For UTF-16BE, a leading FE FF IS a BOM that does not identify the coding scheme, and `remove_bom` removes it.

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-16LE coding scheme IS FF FE.
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: For UTF-16LE, the octet sequence FF FE IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE; comments: no signature meaning

ambiguity.issue: 'no signature meaning' does not say whether FF FE at the start of UTF-16LE data is treated as a ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE character (and therefore kept by `remove_bom`) or is still removed as a BOM; the first reading was chosen as it follows Unicode practice.
readings: For UTF-16LE, a leading FF FE IS NOT a BOM, and `remove_bom` IS NOT required to remove it.
For UTF-16LE, a leading FF FE IS a BOM that does not identify the coding scheme, and `remove_bom` removes it.

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-16 coding scheme IS FE FF or FF FE.
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16; initial octet sequence: FE FF FF FE; comments: signature (default FE FF)

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: For UTF-16, the initial octet sequence IS a signature, and FE FF IS the default initial octet sequence.
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16; initial octet sequence: FE FF FF FE; comments: signature (default FE FF)

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-32BE coding scheme IS 00 00 FE FF.
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32BE; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: For UTF-32BE, the octet sequence 00 00 FE FF IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32BE; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF; comments: no signature meaning

ambiguity.issue: 'no signature meaning' does not say whether 00 00 FE FF at the start of UTF-32BE data is treated as a ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE character (and therefore kept by `remove_bom`) or is still removed as a BOM; the first reading was chosen as it follows Unicode practice.
readings: For UTF-32BE, a leading 00 00 FE FF IS NOT a BOM, and `remove_bom` IS NOT required to remove it.
For UTF-32BE, a leading 00 00 FE FF IS a BOM that does not identify the coding scheme, and `remove_bom` removes it.

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-32LE coding scheme IS FF FE 00 00.
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE 00 00; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: For UTF-32LE, the octet sequence FF FE 00 00 IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE 00 00; comments: no signature meaning

ambiguity.issue: 'no signature meaning' does not say whether FF FE 00 00 at the start of UTF-32LE data is treated as a ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE character (and therefore kept by `remove_bom`) or is still removed as a BOM; the first reading was chosen as it follows Unicode practice.
readings: For UTF-32LE, a leading FF FE 00 00 IS NOT a BOM, and `remove_bom` IS NOT required to remove it.
For UTF-32LE, a leading FF FE 00 00 IS a BOM that does not identify the coding scheme, and `remove_bom` removes it.

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-32 coding scheme IS 00 00 FE FF or FF FE 00 00.
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF FF FE 00 00; comments: signature (default 00 00 FE FF)

requirements.subject: ent:initial-octet-sequence
requirements.canonical: For UTF-32, the initial octet sequence IS a signature, and 00 00 FE FF IS the default initial octet sequence.
requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF FF FE 00 00; comments: signature (default 00 00 FE FF)

requirements.subject: ent:fn-testcasename
requirements.condition: the module control function is executing and no test case is executing
requirements.canonical: When `testcasename` is called while the module control function is executing and no test case is executing, `testcasename` SHALL return the empty string.
requirements.original: When the function testcasename is called if the control part is being executed but no testcase, it shall return the empty string.

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-testcasename
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of predefined functions defined in clause 16.1.2 apply to `testcasename`.
requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-hostid
requirements.canonical: The `hostid` function has the signature `hostid(in charstring idkind := "Ipv4orIPv6") return charstring`, with an `in` formal parameter `idkind` of type `charstring` and a return value of type `charstring`.
requirements.original: hostid(in charstring idkind := "Ipv4orIPv6") return charstring

requirements.subject: ent:idkind-parameter
requirements.condition: no actual parameter is given for idkind
requirements.canonical: If `hostid` is called without an actual parameter, the `idkind` formal parameter IS "Ipv4orIPv6" by default.
requirements.original: hostid(in charstring idkind := "Ipv4orIPv6") return charstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-hostid
requirements.canonical: The `hostid` function SHALL return, as a `charstring`, the host id of the test component or module control function executing the `hostid` function.
requirements.original: The hostid function shall return the host id of the test component or module control executing the hostid function in form of a character string.

ambiguity.issue: 'host id' is not defined; for a host with several addresses of the requested kind it is not stated which one is returned. The reading 'any one address of the executing host' was chosen.
readings: The `hostid` function SHALL return any one address of the requested kind of the host executing the calling component.
The `hostid` function SHALL return the address under which the executing host was addressed (e.g. the host given in `execute`).

requirements.subject: ent:idkind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The `idkind` formal parameter of `hostid` specifies the expected format of the returned host id.
requirements.original: The in parameter idkind allows to specify the expected id format to be returned.

requirements.subject: ent:idkind-parameter
requirements.canonical: The predefined values of the `idkind` formal parameter of `hostid` ARE "Ipv4orIPv6", "Ipv4" and "Ipv6".
requirements.original: Predefined idkind values are:

ambiguity.issue: 'Predefined' suggests that other idkind values may exist, but it is not stated whether other values are tool-specific extensions, yield the empty string, or cause an error. The reading 'other values are implementation-defined' was chosen.
readings: Values of `idkind` other than the predefined ones MAY be supported by a tool with implementation-defined meaning.
Values of `idkind` other than the predefined ones SHALL cause `hostid` to return the empty string.
Values of `idkind` other than the predefined ones SHALL cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-hostid
requirements.condition: idkind is "Ipv4orIPv6" and an Ipv4 address is available
requirements.canonical: If `idkind` is "Ipv4orIPv6" and an Ipv4 address is available, the string returned by `hostid` IS an Ipv4 address.
requirements.original: "Ipv4orIPv6": The contents of the returned character string is an Ipv4 address.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-hostid
requirements.condition: idkind is "Ipv4orIPv6", no Ipv4 address but an Ipv6 address is available
requirements.canonical: If `idkind` is "Ipv4orIPv6" and no Ipv4 address but an Ipv6 address is available, the string returned by `hostid` IS a character string representation of the Ipv6 address.
requirements.original: If no Ipv4 address, but an Ipv6 address is available, a character string representation of the Ipv6 address is returned.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-hostid
requirements.canonical: If `idkind` is "Ipv4", the string returned by `hostid` SHALL be an Ipv4 address.
requirements.original: "Ipv4": The contents of the returned character string shall be an Ipv4 address.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-hostid
requirements.canonical: If `idkind` is "Ipv6", the string returned by `hostid` SHALL be an Ipv6 address.
requirements.original: "Ipv6": The contents of the returned character string shall be an Ipv6 address.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-hostid
requirements.condition: no host id can be retrieved
requirements.canonical: If `hostid` cannot retrieve any host id, `hostid` SHALL return the empty string.
requirements.original: The hostid function shall return the empty string, if it cannot retrieve any host id or a host id of a kind different from the kind defined by the actual idkind parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-hostid
requirements.condition: only a host id of a kind different from idkind can be retrieved
requirements.canonical: If `hostid` can retrieve only a host id of a kind different from the kind given by the `idkind` actual parameter, `hostid` SHALL return the empty string.
requirements.original: The hostid function shall return the empty string, if it cannot retrieve any host id or a host id of a kind different from the kind defined by the actual idkind parameter.

ambiguity.issue: The phrase 'cannot retrieve ... a host id of a kind different from the kind defined by idkind' literally negates the intended condition; the reading 'can retrieve only a host id of a different kind' was chosen.
readings: `hostid` SHALL return the empty string if no host id of the kind given by `idkind` can be retrieved.
`hostid` SHALL return the empty string if no host id of a kind different from `idkind` can be retrieved.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-hostid
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of predefined functions defined in clause 16.1.2 apply to `hostid`.
requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.
